# Hippius

> Hippius is a distributed cloud: encrypted file storage (Drive), S3-compatible object storage, a registry for AI models and containers (Hub), a CDN, and confidential compute (VMs, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes, GitHub Actions runners). One account pays for all of them. From a terminal, `hipc` is the one command for the whole account. This file says how an agent gets set up, what each product is, and which file to open next.

Open only the file for the product you need. The long reference for the whole product, including the S3 manual, is [llms-full.txt](https://docs.hippius.com/llms-full.txt)

## If you can run commands, use hipc first

Use `hipc` first for anything on the account API: accounts and projects, billing, storage keys and buckets, Hub, compute and App Engine, CDN, network, and support.

- Install: `brew install thenervelab/tap/hipc`, or `curl -fsSL https://github.com/thenervelab/hippius-cli/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`. On PyPI the package is `hippius` and the command it installs is `hipc`: `pip install hippius`, `uv tool install hippius`, or `pipx install hippius` installs the same binary.
- Log in with the token the user gives you: `hipc auth login --token-file -` (paste it, Enter, Ctrl-D), then `hipc auth status`. At their own terminal the user can also run plain `hipc auth login`, which asks for the token without showing it. Never ask for the token in the chat; the user runs this on their machine. Where the token comes from: https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/settings after a Google, GitHub or Apple sign-in; for a 12-word access key account, `hipc auth login --access-key`; see Account, sign-in, and paying, below.
- Run `hipc schema` to discover every command, its effect, confirmations and error codes. The whole document is large (about 160 KB): `hipc schema <path…>`, such as `hipc schema compute vms` or `hipc schema s3 buckets create`, lists only the commands under that path, in the same shape.
- Output is JSON on a pipe, with `CI`, or with `AI_AGENT=1`.
- `--dry-run` sends nothing. A write that spends, deletes, revokes, rotates or cancels needs `--yes` (`CI` and `AI_AGENT` never stand in for it); a secret needs `--reveal`, or a flag that writes it to a private file: `--secret-file` and `--credentials-dir` count as the reveal; `--reveal` alone prints the secret on stdout.
- Exit 0 success, 1 the API or runtime failed, 2 fix the invocation (nothing that changes state was sent). A failure is one JSON object on stderr; branch on `error.code`.
- No command for it: `hipc api <METHOD> <PATH>`, e.g. `hipc api GET /accounts/` (sent under /api), before any direct call to https://api.hippius.com.

More: [For agents](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents) (raw: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-cli/main/docs/agents.md), [Examples](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/examples), [Command reference](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/commands).

## Which file to open

| Want to | Open |
|---|---|
| Manage the account, projects, billing, plans, S3 buckets and keys, Hub, compute and App Engine apps, Kubernetes, databases, runners, CDN, the private network, or support from a terminal or an agent | [hipc](https://docs.hippius.com/cli), as above |
| Store or fetch files from code, rclone, or a backup tool | [hippius-s3 llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-s3/staging/llms.txt) |
| Store encrypted files in the browser (Drive) | [Drive guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/drive) |
| Back up photos or a folder from a computer or phone | Drive with the [desktop app](https://docs.hippius.com/use/desktop/getting-started) or the Android app; first steps under Account, sign-in, and paying, below |
| Publish or pull a model or a container image | [hippius-hub llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-hub/main/llms.txt); the namespace, plan, and CI keys are also `hipc hub` |
| Sync folders on a computer | [hippius-desktop llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-desktop/staging/llms.txt) |
| Work in a shared drive | A Drive someone else owns and invited you into. They pay for the storage. It shows in the console under Storage after the invite. |
| Give a coding agent shared memory | [hippius-mem llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-mem/main/llms.txt) |
| Script Drive with encryption on the client | [hippius-drive-sdk llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-drive-sdk/main/llms.txt) |
| Sign up, pay, get an API token, or manage Drive and S3 keys in the browser | [Console getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/getting-started) |
| Use Drive on an Android phone | [Mobile getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/mobile/getting-started) |
| Run a VM, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes or GitHub Actions runners (Compute) | `hipc compute`, and the [Compute guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute) |
| Serve an S3 bucket through the CDN (zones on <zone>.c.hipcdn.net or your own domain; FR $0.010/GB, AU $0.060/GB, $0.002 per 10,000 requests, $1/month per custom domain) | `hipc cdn`, and the [CDN guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/cdn) |
| Filter requests to a CDN zone with a WAF: custom rules, rate limits, IP/ASN/country lists (every zone, Security tab; Standard $5, Advanced $20 per zone per month) | `hipc cdn waf`, and the [WAF guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/cdn/firewall) |
| Read compute, CDN, S3, Drive and Hub prices without an account (`hipc compute public-prices`, `hipc s3 plans`, or GET https://api.hippius.com/api/compute/public-prices/, no auth), or sign users in with their 12-word access key from your own app | [Management API](https://docs.hippius.com/use/api), which links the Public Price API and Access Key Sign-In API pages |
| Let team members use your compute, S3 and CDN, or work in an account you were invited to (shared accounts) | `hipc account list`, `hipc account use <account_id>`, and the [Shared accounts guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/team) |
| Run a storage miner | [Miner guide](https://docs.hippius.com/earn/arion/running-miner) and [arion llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/arion/main/llms.txt) |
| Run a validator | [Validator guide](https://docs.hippius.com/earn/installing-validator) |

## Account, sign-in, and paying

Full console guide: [Console getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/getting-started)
Billing: [Billing guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing)

- One account covers the console, the desktop app, the mobile app, and `hipc`. Sign-in is Google, GitHub, Apple, or an existing 12-word access key. There is no email and password sign-in.
- The API token, for Hub, the account API and `hipc`, depends on how the user signs in:
  - Google, GitHub or Apple: the user copies it from console Settings, https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/settings, and stores it with `hipc auth login` as above. An agent cannot do this sign-in for them.
  - A 12-word access key: Settings does not show a token for this sign-in. The access-key sign-in (https://docs.hippius.com/use/wallet-login) signs a challenge with the key and returns a token, and its first verify creates the account. Run `hipc auth login --access-key` on the user's own machine. A phrase the API has not seen opens a new, empty account, and so does one mistyped word: when the verify answers `is_new`, `hipc auth login` exits 2 and stores no token, but the server has already opened that empty account. Pass `--new-account` when a new account is meant. A later login with the same words logs in to the account the server opened. The login asks for the 12 words at a prompt that does not show them, or reads them with `--access-key-file <path|->`, signs the challenge, and stores only the token; the API flow is the alternative for an app. Never ask for the 12 words in chat.
  - For CI or a server, sign in once on a machine you trust and store only the token (as the secret `HIPPIUS_TOKEN`). Never put the 12 words on a runner: they control the whole account and its funds.
- A 12-word access key creates a wallet-only account. It has no real email address, so it gets no lifecycle mail. Drive has no free plan: subscribe before the first upload. S3 and Hub work the same as on any other account.
- S3 endpoint is https://s3.hippius.com only. Keys (the access key id starts with `hip_`) are created with `hipc s3 tokens create`, or on the console S3 page: https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/s3. For an app, prefer a sub token scoped to its bucket: `hipc --json s3 tokens create --kind sub --name app --scope-type single-bucket --bucket <bucket> --action read --action write --secret-file s3.secret --yes > token.json`. `--secret-file` writes the secret alone (no newline) to a new mode-0600 file, and the JSON names it as `secret_file` in place of the secret, so the secret never reaches a log or your transcript. A master token (`--kind master`) reaches every bucket and bypasses bucket ACLs. `hipc s3 configure --from-token-file token.json` writes an AWS CLI profile from it, reading the secret from the `secret_file` path relative to the current directory, so run it where the create ran; delete s3.secret and token.json after.
- Hub has a second credential, the registry robot login, created when the namespace is provisioned (`hipc --json hub namespace create <namespace> --secret-file robot.secret --yes > robot.json`, whose answer names the file as `robot_secret_file`, or `hippius-hub`). For CI, create a scoped key instead of sharing that login: `hipc --json hub keys create --name ci --role push --secret-file key.secret --yes > key.json`; its answer holds `login` and `secret_file`, and `docker login registry.hippius.com -u '<login>' --password-stdin < key.secret` logs in. Single-quote the login: it contains a `$`. `hipc hub keys rotate` and `hipc hub namespace robot rotate` take `--secret-file` too. GitHub Actions: https://docs.hippius.com/registry/ci
- Drive encryption uses an unlock password and a 12-word recovery seed. Never ask the user to paste either into chat.
- 1 credit = $1: a price or cap given in credits, such as `--monthly-cap`, is in dollars. 1 USDC adds one dollar to your balance. Topping up fills the balance. It does not add storage. Subscribe to a plan for that. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing
- Top up on Billing in one of five ways. Card, through Stripe, from $10 to $10,000, or a monthly auto reload (`hipc billing top-up --amount 10 --method card --yes` prints the checkout URL; `hipc billing auto-reload update`). Bitcoin, on-chain or Lightning, from $20 to $100,000. Lightning lands in seconds; on-chain after one confirmation. USDC on Base from a browser wallet, from $5 to $10,000; 1 USDC adds one dollar to your balance. TAO, from a connected wallet or by sending to the TAO deposit address (Manually tab), at least $20 per transfer; never send TAO to the Hippius account address, which is not credited. A transfer cannot be reversed. hAlpha (Hippius native token), on the Hippius tab: credits = hAlpha × the on-chain hAlpha price, 1% slippage protection by default, final on chain with no refund. `hipc billing top-up` takes card, Bitcoin, or hAlpha. `hipc billing native-quote` shows the hAlpha price, `min_alpha`, `native_balance`, and `custodial`. When `custodial` is true (the API signs the account's buys), `hipc billing top-up --method halpha --alpha 1.5 --yes` converts hAlpha into credits on chain: at least 0.01 hAlpha, with a minimum of 1% less than the quoted credits, and it cannot be undone. An account that signs its own buys (`custodial` false, such as an access-key account) still buys in the console, and USDC and TAO stay in the console. Those are browser wallet steps a person approves, so an agent cannot fund the balance with them on its own. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing
- An agent with enough balance subscribes without a browser: `hipc drive subscription subscribe --plan solo --yes` (codes `solo` Starter, `duo` Plus, `max`, `scale`; `--period monthly|annual`; `subscribe` is for an account on Free or no plan: to move a paid plan to another, `hipc drive subscription change --plan duo --yes`, and `hipc s3 subscription change` likewise), `hipc s3 subscription subscribe --plan pro --yes` (codes `pro`, `business`, `enterprise`), `hipc hub subscription subscribe --plan Builder --yes` (names Free, Builder, Pro, Team; paid from the balance only; a second paid plan needs `--replace`). Run each with `--dry-run` first. The plan lists are `hipc drive plans`, `hipc s3 plans`, `hipc hub plans`, with no token. Card checkout is a browser; do not send a funded agent there.
- Google, GitHub, and Apple accounts include the Free Drive Plan (10 GB). S3 starts on pay as you go at $6 per TB per month, and a plan is optional.
- First steps for a new account that wants to back up photos or a folder: the Free plan's 10 GB is there at once (a 12-word access key account has none); for more, top up at least $10 on Billing, then `hipc drive subscription subscribe --plan solo --yes` (Starter, 500 GB, $4 a month); then install the desktop app (https://docs.hippius.com/use/desktop/getting-started) or the Android app and sign in there. Drive uploads happen in those apps and need no API token; ask for a token only to read the plan or subscribe from `hipc`.
- Plan prices, monthly, from the balance (always current in the catalogs): Drive Free 10 GB $0, Starter 500 GB $4, Plus 2 TB $7, Max 10 TB $22, Scale 25 TB $50 (Max and Scale bill storage above the plan hourly, $2.20 and $2.00 per TB per month, up to a storage cap that defaults to twice the plan). S3 Pro 10 TB $53, Business 50 TB $245, Enterprise 100 TB $465 (pay as you go otherwise: $6 per TB per month). Hub Free $0, Builder $5, Pro $19, Team $99.
- Shared accounts: an owner invites members by email, with Viewer, Operator or Admin access per product (VMs, databases, Kubernetes, runners, S3, CDN). The owner pays and the owner's quotas apply. Drive is not included. `hipc account list` shows the accounts a token can act in; `hipc account use <account_id>` or `--account <account_id>` acts in one. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/team
- Open a support ticket: `hipc support tickets create --subject <text> --body-file <path> --yes`.

Hub Free plan: creating a namespace requires a balance of at least $10, a spam check. A zero balance is refused. The plan price stays zero. Top up, then provision. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/hub

## Without hipc: the raw API

The OpenAPI spec is https://api.hippius.com/swagger.json. Header `Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN`, plus `X-Hippius-Account: acct_...` for a shared account (ids from GET https://api.hippius.com/api/accounts/). Subscribe routes: POST https://api.hippius.com/api/drive/subscription/ with `{"plan":"solo","period":"monthly","payment":"credits"}`; POST https://api.hippius.com/api/s3/subscription/ with `{"plan":"pro","rail":"credits"}`; GET https://api.hippius.com/api/registry/plans/ then POST https://api.hippius.com/api/registry/subscribe/ with `{"plan_id": 2}` (the API requires `plan_id`, not a name; Builder is id 2). 201 if the balance covers the plan. Support: POST https://api.hippius.com/api/support/tickets/ with subject, priority, category, and description. Send your own User-Agent: some default ones (Python urllib) are blocked with 403 error 1010.

## Deprecated

The IPFS-era command line (its `hipc storage` commands; the name `hipc` now belongs to the new CLI above), `hippius-sdk`, `hippius-sdk-ts`, `hippius-sdk-rust`, `hippius-rust-sdk`, `hippius-sync-engine`, `hippius-storage-miner`, the storage commands of the Python package `hippius` up to 0.2.77, and anything else IPFS-related, are deprecated. Hippius switched from IPFS to Arion. https://docs.hippius.com/cli/usage

Chain registration still uses the Python package `hippius` pinned to `hippius==0.2.77`: https://docs.hippius.com/earn/register-in-blockchain

## Compute

Confidential VMs on AMD SEV-SNP, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes and GitHub Actions runners, open to every account. Metered per second (one-minute minimum per VM and public IPv4), charged hourly on the Hippius chain from the account balance. A VM is billed from its launch until it is deleted, running or stopped. A launch needs a balance covering 24 hours of the account's compute plus the launch (`hipc billing summary`: `balance` in dollars and `burn_rate_per_hour` in base units, 10^18 = $1; the launch passes when balance ≥ runway hours from `hipc compute quota` (24) × (burn rate + the new item's hourly price from `hipc compute prices`); https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/billing#the-24-hour-balance-requirement), and quotas apply: new accounts start on the Starter tier and move up automatically with their charged usage.

An hour the balance cannot pay is recorded as unpaid debt that the account owes, and VMs keep running: the balance is not a spending cap. To limit what a project spends in a month, set a budget. The Default project has no budget: create a project (`hipc account projects create --name api`), launch in it (`--project <project_id>`, or `hipc account projects use <project_id>` first), then `hipc account projects budget update <project_id> --monthly-limit 25 --alert-at 80 --block-launches true --yes` mails at each `--alert-at` share and, with `--block-launches true`, refuses new launches that add cost once the limit is reached. It does not stop what already runs, which keeps being billed. `hipc compute charge-cap` is the most the chain charges the account per hour, a safety limit, not a monthly budget.

From a terminal: `hipc compute flavors`, `hipc compute regions`, `hipc compute images`, `hipc compute quota`, then `hipc compute vms create --flavor small --name web-1 --image <image> --public-ip --ssh-public-key-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --dry-run` and the same with `--yes`; `hipc compute vms get <vm_id>` follows it to `running`. A VM launched by hipc has no firewall rule, so nothing reaches its public IPv4 until a port is opened: `--open-ssh` (port 22) or `--open-port 443` on `vms create` opens a TCP port to every IPv4 address right after the launch; to limit the sources, `hipc compute firewall update <vm_id> --rules-file rules.json --yes` replaces the rules, with a file such as `{"rules":[{"protocol":"tcp","ports":["22"],"source_cidrs":["203.0.113.7/32"],"description":"ssh"},{"protocol":"tcp","ports":["80","443"],"description":"web"}]}`. To attach an IPv4 later: `hipc compute public-ip create <vm_id> --yes`. `hipc compute vms delete <vm_id> --yes` releases the public IPv4 with the VM (no detach first; it is billed until then); stored backups stay billed until they are removed. `hipc compute ssh-keys create --name laptop --public-key-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --yes` stores a key for `--ssh-key-id`. Databases are `hipc compute databases`, Kubernetes `hipc compute kubernetes`, runners `hipc compute runners`. `hipc compute prices` and `hipc compute public-prices` are the live price list.

Prices per 730-hour month, on the default NVMe OS disk: vCPU $18, memory $2.50/GB, disk $0.10/GB. Small (1 vCPU, 4 GB, 40 GB) is $32 a month ($0.0438/h), Medium $64, Large $128, X-Large $256, 2X-Large $512, 4X-Large $1024. The OS disk tier is chosen at launch and fixed: SSD (disk $0.06/GB, Small $27.60, Medium $55.20, Large $110.40) or HDD, slow shared storage for dev and test, not for production or databases, offered up to Large (disk $0.03/GB, Small $17.16, Medium $34.32, Large $68.64). Dedicated disks (whole physical disks for one VM, up to 8, at least 1,000 GiB each; the VM is then pinned: no backups, migration or failover): $2.50 HDD, $5 SSD, $8 NVMe per TiB-month. Public IPv4 $0.005/h (~$3.65/month). VM backups $6 per TB-month. Outbound bandwidth is metered per region and not charged today; inbound is free. Managed databases cost their VMs plus 25%; Kubernetes costs its VMs plus $15 per cluster per month. The live price list wins: https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/billing/compute#prices

- Overview (quotas, the 24-hour balance requirement, billing): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute
- Create a VM and connect over SSH or from the browser: https://docs.hippius.com/use/virtual-machines
- Public IPv4, firewall rules and published ports: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/networking
- Resize a VM (vCPU and memory; the disk is kept): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/resize
- VM backups and restore: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-backups
- Dedicated disks (whole physical HDD/SSD/NVMe disks, exact tier, pinned VM, own quota): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/dedicated-disks
- VM failover: if a VM's server dies, the VM restarts on another server in the same region from its latest backup, keeping its IP and NetBird address; data since that backup is lost. Automatic failover is opt-in per VM, at creation (switch under Automatic backups; API `"failover_mode": "auto"` with `backup_interval_s`) or later in the Backups panel. Offered in France only today. Active after the first full backup: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-failover
- Placement groups: VMs of one account in the same group (`placement_group` at creation, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9, -) are never on the same server. A different server is not a different datacenter. Fixed at creation: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-failover#placement-groups
- Compute API, only without hipc: base https://api.hippius.com/api, header `Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN` (plus `X-Hippius-Account: acct_...` for a shared account). Full OpenAPI spec: https://api.hippius.com/swagger.json. Create a VM with POST /api/compute/vms/ `{"name":"web-1","flavor":"small","region":"FR","ssh_key_ids":[123]}` (keys from GET /api/ssh-keys/), then poll GET /api/compute/vms/<vm_id>/ until `status` is `running` and, with a public IPv4, `network_ready` is `true`, then SSH to the public IP (or to `netbird_ip` over NetBird). `status` is the lifecycle (billed while `running`, stopped included), `power_state` is on/off: https://docs.hippius.com/use/api#compute-api
- Managed PostgreSQL 16/17/18 (one-time credentials, TLS, backups to your S3, restore, HA failover): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/databases
- Managed Kubernetes clusters (cluster key, kubeconfig, API access): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes
- Kubernetes worker pools and signed node operations: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes-worker-pools
- Kubernetes backups (etcd snapshots, Velero, restore with rclone): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes-backups
- GitHub Actions runners (`runs-on: hippius-small|medium|large`, `-ssd` for the cheaper SSD tier; spend per day, repository, size and workflow, compared with GitHub-hosted runners): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/runners
- Compute prices, management fees, quotas and unpaid balance: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/billing
- Refusals and troubleshooting: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/troubleshooting

The Kubernetes cluster key is generated in the user's browser, so creating a cluster stays in the console; hipc lists, reads and deletes clusters, scales node pools and writes kubeconfigs. Database credentials are returned once at creation, and the server keeps no copy. Always pass `--credentials-dir`, so no secret reaches stdout or a transcript: `mkdir -m 700 ~/db && hipc compute databases create --tier starter --size s --engine-version 17 --yes --credentials-dir ~/db` writes five new 0600 files there: `client.crt`, `client.key`, `ca.crt`, `credentials.json` (the whole credentials object, password and backup passphrase included), and `.env` (`PGUSER`, `PGPASSWORD`, `PGDATABASE`, `PGSSLMODE`, the three TLS paths, absolute; `PGHOST` and `PGPORT` when the answer has them). stdout keeps only the username, the database, `shown_once`, and the file paths. Connect with `cd ~/db; set -a; . ./.env; set +a; psql "host=<address from hipc compute databases get>"`. `hipc compute databases restore` takes `--credentials-dir` the same way. `hipc compute databases delete` cannot be undone, and a deleted database cannot be restored: take a `pg_dump` first. Never ask the user to paste a database secret into chat.
